subject: MAP cadence re-scope: stabilization sprint & revised close cadence
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@averyhealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP cadence re-scope: stabilization sprint & revised close cadence

Sarah —

Thanks again for the candid call this morning. We heard you: the evaluation window compressed materially, and the internal procurement hold slowed the SSO/INFRA approvals. I put a very short stabilization plan together (attached MAP_v4.xlsx) that focuses on three practical moves over the next two weeks to get to a viable go/no-go by 09/07.

High-level ask: can your team confirm acceptance criteria on the security/eval checklist (page 2) and confirm a single procurement approver that can clear the SOW when we ship the final revisions? If procurement needs a DocuSign stub earlier, we can provide a redline-friendly SOW draft (SOW_draft_20270823.pdf).

What we'll do on our side:
- Freeze the model variant for the eval (no further model swaps during the sprint).
- Stand up a dedicated test harness on your VPC for two days to capture perf KPIs.
- Prioritize the KV-cache profile you flagged (low-latency pref).

I cc'd Jordan and Kimberly — Jordan will run the stabilization sprint and Kimberly will coordinate procurement touches. Please let me know which of the proposed checkpoints in the MAP work for your team.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0137
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_v4.xlsx (spreadsheet), SOW_draft_20270823.pdf (document)

From: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@averyhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Avery Health Procurement <procurement@averyhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP cadence re-scope: stabilization sprint & revised close cadence

Marcus —

Appreciate the quick synthesis and the concrete checkpoints. Short answers: procurement put the SOW on hold pending a security snapshot (SOC-2 artifact + data flow diagram) and a clearer acceptance test for latency under our typical payload. I can confirm our acceptance criteria on page 2 by EOD tomorrow (Aug 24). Procurement pointed me to Lisa (procurement@averyhealth.com) who is the approver — I looped the mailbox above.

Two things from our side that caused the slip: 1) our infra team found an unexpected IP egress policy that blocked the initial test harness; 2) a clinical reviewer requested an extra privacy review because some sample data included PII in notes. We need the stabilization sprint to explicitly show zero egress and sanitized evaluation data.

We can do the two-day harness on Aug 30–31 if that works for your ops team. DocuSign on a redline-friendly SOW is helpful — please mark any non-negotiable clauses (data residency, audit logs).

—Sarah
Sarah Patel
Head of Data & Analytics | Avery Health
sarah.patel@averyhealth.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP cadence re-scope: stabilization sprint & revised close cadence

Team —

Packing a short internal runbook for the stabilization sprint. Action items I'm assigning here (internal only):
1) Marcus: get Sarah the SOC-2 snapshot + data flow diagram by EOD Aug 23 (I can pull the sanitized diagrams).
2) Kimberly: prepare the Procurement one-pager and highlight the clauses we'll treat as negotiable vs. hard stop (data residency, audit access).
3) Me: set up a dedicated ephemeral test harness in us-west2 for Aug 30–31; will provide the ingress whitelist and a live test script.

Risk callouts: if the privacy reviewer requires a third-party redaction audit, that adds a 7–10 business day delay. We should preempt that by providing a sanitized sample set and an isolation checklist. I put notes in the MAP_v4.xlsx under "risk mitigations".

I'll open a short Slack channel #avy-map with the ops folks so we can triage in real time. Marcus — can you confirm whether Avery will accept our sanitized sample set format (CSV + redacted notes) or they need a synthetic generator?

Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@averyhealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP cadence re-scope: stabilization sprint & revised close cadence

Sarah —

Confirmed: we can provide the SOC-2 snapshot and an isolated redacted sample set in the format you requested (CSV + redacted notes) by EOD Aug 24. Kimberly — please attach the procurement one-pager and the redlineable SOW to the thread once available. Marissa, looping you to flag for potential exec intervention — if procurement holds beyond Aug 27 we should consider a small concession (one-week credit) to preserve the close timeline.

Proposed revised cadence (short):
- Aug 24: finalize acceptance criteria (Avery) + Redwood delivers SOC-2 snapshot + sanitized samples
- Aug 30–31: stabilization sprint (ops) — live metrics capture
- Sep 01: joint evaluation review; procurement to return SOW decision or request a final revision
- Sep 07: go/no-go decision and target close if procurement clears

If the privacy reviewer requests extra audit, we escalate to Marissa and request procurement to run in parallel with their legal review (to avoid serial gating).

Thanks,
Marcus

Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 04:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP cadence re-scope: stabilization sprint & revised close cadence

All —

Thanks for the plan. Quick executive note on escalation and trade-offs: if Procurement needs extra legal review and requests contract-level redlines that materially change our data-residency terms, we should treat that as a formal scope change and schedule a short pricing review. To keep the deal from slipping, I'm authorizing a one-time operational credit (2 weeks of reserved capacity) that Marcus can offer to Avery in exchange for running procurement and legal reviews in parallel (not serial).

Marcus — you have my OK to present the credit as a conditional concession that expires Aug 30 COB. Use language that preserves our standard SLA and audit language; procurement must acknowledge that the credit is a one-time operational make-good.

I'll monitor — ping me if the privacy reviewer asks for a third-party audit.

Marissa Cole
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
